subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto, and what fail-closed ordering should it use around validation, SecretRef preflight, and persistence?
rationale: This would create a new plugin API that can block persisted configuration writes, so automation should not choose the security boundary or permanent contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design the veto API
options.body: Proceed through the config validation/mutation RFC with a narrow hook contract covering all config mutation paths before disk writes.

options.title: Keep validation internal
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers want config safety handled only by built-in validation, tool allowlists, and doctor/preflight checks.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight
options.body: Defer this issue behind the standardized preflight framework if maintainers want one unified validation mechanism rather than a config-specific hook.

recommendation.title: Design the veto API
recommendation.body: Proceed through the config validation/mutation RFC with a narrow hook contract covering all config mutation paths before disk writes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the maintainer-facing review tying this issue to the RFC direction.
